MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 26, 2026
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Riggins called the meeting to order at 4:32 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Marianne Riggins; Mayor Pro Tern Bruce Silverstein; and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, and Steve Uhring.

  ABSENT: Councilmember Doug Stewart

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Anne K.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 4:35 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Liability Claims Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.95(a)

  I.  Claimant: Adrian Fernandez
  Agency claimed against: City of Malibu

Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
54956.9(d)(1):

  1.  Fernandez v. City of Malibu et al., LASC Case No. 24STCV30411

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

  1.  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Government
  Code section 54956.9
  Number of potential cases: (2)

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Riggins called the meeting to order at 5:38 p.m.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 2 of 12

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Marianne Riggins; Mayor Pro Tern Bruce Silverstein; and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, and Steve Uhring.

  ABSENT: Councilmember Doug Stewart

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Rob DuBoux, Interim City
  Manager; Christopher Smith, Assistant City Manager; Frances Arricale, Deputy City
  Manager; Richard Rojas, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin
  Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Community Development
  Director; Tatiana Holden, Interim Public Works Director; Susan Duefias, Public Safety
  Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Christina Mutioz, Deputy City Clerk; Nausicaa
  Smith, Administrative Assistant; Tyler Eaton, Assistant Community Development
  Director; Brandie Ayala, Senior Management Analyst; Travis Hart, Interim Assistant
  Public Works Director; and Julie Santia, Associate Engineer.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Riggins led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 4:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.95(a), and 54956.9, with all Councilmembers present, except Councilmember
  Stewart. He stated the Council discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took
  no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  January 15, 2026, with the amended agenda posted on January 23, 2026.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The motion carried 4-0, Councilmember Stewart absent.

ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Anne K.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 3 of 12

  As there were no other speakers present for the Consent Calendar, the Mayor
  returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  Item Nos. 1.B.3. and 1.B.5. were pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Mayor Riggins seconded a motion to approve
  the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 1.B.3. and 1.B.5. The motion carried 4-0,
  Councilmember Stewart absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  77650-77868 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 782 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $8,677,543.35. City of Malibu payroll check number 5546-5556 and
  ACH deposits were issued in the amount of $1,733,136.24.
  4.  Professional Services Agreements for On-Call Publishing, Printing, and
  Mailing Consulting Services
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute a professional
  services agreement with Earth Print, Inc. (DBA CR Print) to provide on-call
  publishing, printing, and mailing consulting services; and 2) Authorize the
  Mayor to execute a professional services agreement with Brian Shore (DBA
  Totalgraphics) to provide on-call printing consulting services.
  6.  Professional Services Agreement for FEMA and CalOES assistance
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute a Professional
  Services Agreement with DCMC, LLC., for FEMA and CalOES assistance.
  7.  Investment Report for the Month Ending November 30, 2025
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month
  ending November 30, 2025.
  8.  Professional Services Agreement Amendment No. 3 with Quinto
  Consulting, LP for City Treasurer Services and Request for Proposals
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No.
  3 to the Professional Services Agreement with Quinto Consulting, LP for
  City Treasurer services to extend the term of the agreement; 2) Direct the
  City Manager to develop and issue a request for proposals (RFP) for future
  City Treasurer services; and 3) Assign the Administration and Finance
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 4 of 12

  Subcommittee to review the proposals, conduct interviews, and make a
  recommendation to City Council regarding the selection of City Treasurer.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the June 25, 2025 Special
  Meeting, June 26, 2025 Special Meeting, July 3, 2025 Special Meeting, July
  10, 2025 Special Meeting, July 11, 2025 Special Meeting.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Mayor Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the minutes for the June 25, 2025 Special Meeting, June 26, 2025
  Special Meeting, July 3, 2025 Special Meeting, July 11, 2025 Special
  Meeting. The motion carried 4-0, Councilmember Stewart absent.

  5.  Amendment to Agreement with Integrated Performance Consultants, Inc.
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 4
  to the Professional Services Agreement with Integrated Performance
  Consultants, Inc. (IPC) for operation and maintenance services of the Civic
  Center Water Treatment Facility (CCWTF) extending the term of the
  Agreement for one additional year.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved to authorize the Mayor to execute
  Amendment No. 4 to the Professional Services Agreement with Integrated
  Performance Consultants, Inc. (IPC) for operation and maintenance services
  of the Civic Center Water Treatment Facility (CCWTF), extending the term
  of the Agreement for one additional year.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  Councilmember Conrad seconded the motion.

  The motion carried 4-0, Councilmember Stewart absent.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Interim City Manager DuBoux announced Small Business Administration (SBA)
  disaster loan outreach center hours, a Habitat for Humanity workshop, the ribbon
  cutting for the Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) Signal Synchronization Project, a fire
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 5 of 12

  rebuild design professionals workshop, the City Hall closure for Presidents Day,
  and a household ha72rdous waste collection event. He also reported on the Los
  Angeles County homeless count and statistics for Malibu.

  Community Development Director Bundy presented an update on fire rebuild
  statistics. She presented information on City of Los Angeles rebuild statistics and
  stated it was not clear how many homes had been fully permitted to rebuild. She
  discussed staffs research into Building Code Section 110.2.3.6 and restrictions on
  who may rebuild in an active landslide area after a disaster. She stated she had
  spoken with Los Angeles County staff and explained the County's interpretation
  and process for permitting rebuilds for properties that had been sold to new owners.
  She explained that the City would follow a similar process.

  The Council directed questions to Community Development Director Bundy.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriffs Department, discussed
  significant incidents from the last month.

  Deputy Carlos Vindell, Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department School Resource
  Officer, provided an update on school-related incidents and resources made
  available to the school community.

  The Council directed questions to Deputy Vindell about enforcement issues related
  to the school.

  Officer Jason Lopez, California Highway Patrol (CHP), presented an update and
  statistics regarding the CHP Task Force patrol program for 2026 and since
  inception.

  The Council directed questions to Officer Lopez regarding program reporting and
  Task Force operations.

  Ranger Tim Pera, Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority (MRCA),
  presented the monthly ranger report.

  James Latham, MRCA Chief of Operations, discussed operations during the last
  two weekends of warm weather. He discussed plans to install cameras on MRCA
  property to support ranger activities.

  In response to Interim City Attorney Rusin, Mr. Latham confirmed the MRCA
  would apply for the appropriate permits and collaborate with the City's Public
  Safety Department.

  The Council directed questions to Mr. Latham regarding visitor Counts and off-trail
  enforcement.

CONSENSUS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 6 of 12

  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item on the current policy
  on Commissioner Updates and consider providing additional direction to the
  Commissions on the appropriate interval for updates.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Michel Shane announced a February 9, 2026 safe driving program with AAA at
  Malibu High School and discussed a potential enforcement program to address
  excessive speeding.

  Darren Graves commended Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein and Councilmember
  Conrad for efforts on the January 12, 2026 Item No. 8.A. report and discussed the
  importance of adopting that resolution.

  Kevin Keegan discussed the Pier to Pier ferry proposal and provided updates on the
  enterprise.

  Jason Riddick, Malibu West Homeowners Association, provided an update
  regarding the Broad Beach Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD)
  litigation.

  Men! May discussed ways to improve PCH striping and safety near Escondido.

  Jack Gladney discussed the Code Enforcement violations on Councilmember
  Uhring's property. He discussed Commissioner John Ma s comments at the last
  Planning Commission meeting.

  Anne K. discussed cougars in town and her campaign for governor.

  Terry Davis requested the City send a letter of support for sales tax relief for fire
  rebuild materials. She requested the City of Malibu participate in the water
  infrastructure improvements discussions.

  Danny discussed Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) interpretations
  of some seawalls as obstructions. He requested an update on how beachfront
  rebuilds with seawalls would be permitted.

ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Uhring stated he met with a member of the Zuru team regarding
  plans to rebuild properties in Malibu using modular homes. He announced that
  Keegan Gibbs would be leaving the Public Safety Commission and encouraged
  interested individuals to apply. He discussed complaints he had received regarding
  food trucks and stated staff was working on an ordinance to improve food truck
  enforcement. He discussed a presentation from Santa Monica-Malibu Unified
  School District (SM-MUSD) at the Planning Commission regarding demolition
  plans at Malibu High School. He suggested the City consider whether temporary
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 7 of 12

trailers could be repurposed by the City. He suggested organizing a community
picnic to bring the community together after multiple disasters.

Mayor Riggins indicated support for organizing a community picnic if there was
interest from the community.

Councilmember Conrad stated she had encouraged the residents to organize and
hold community events.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated he
would request additional information from SM-MUSD regarding its demolition
plans.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux discussed
the City's street vendor ordinance and explained staff was looking for ordinance
options to better manage food trucks in the City.

Councilmember Conrad discussed ongoing issues in the City that are challenged by
multiple agencies having jurisdiction, such as the Zuma Beach underpass closure.
She suggested considering an ordinance or fine structure to encourage more timely
improvements by other agencies with property within City limits.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux discussed
the City's collaborative efforts with Supervisor Horvath's Office and Los Angeles
County Beaches and Harbors to improve and reopen the Zuma Beach underpass.
He stated City staff continued to work with Supervisor Horvath's Office and the
relevant agencies on this issue.

Councilmember Conrad asked which agency owned the changeable message signs
on PCH. She recommended that signs not in use be removed or used for other public
communications.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Attorney Rusin discussed
ways the proposed Pier to Pier ferry plan could come before the Council.

Councilmember Conrad discussed the importance of working with Los Angeles
County Beaches and Harbors to improve the maintenance of the beaches in the City
and recommended appointing an ad hoc committee or liaison. She suggested
advertising Charmlee Park as an alternative hiking site to Escondido Trail.

In response to Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein, City Clerk Pettijohn explained that ad
hoc committees could only be formed for a specific purpose and that subcommittees
formed with an ongoing subject matter jurisdiction would be subject to the Brown
Act.

Councilmember Conrad discussed an upcoming meeting regarding approval of
funding for improved septic systems at Malibu beaches.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 8 of 12

  In response to Mayor Riggins, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated any
  Councilmembers could send letters of support as individuals for the upcoming
  meeting.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to discuss options
  on how the City Council could better interface with Los Angeles County Beaches
  and Harbors and other partner agencies with open space in the City.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad and Mayor Riggins, Interim City Manager
  DuBoux stated staff would bring forward an item on February 23, 2026 to address
  the FEMA seawall issue raised during public comment.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein, Interim City Manager DuBoux
  explained that a variance under FEMA's development standards is separate from,
  and has different findings than, a coastal development permit (CDP) variance.

  Councilmember Conrad requested that the January 12, 2026 Item No. 8.A. report
  be rescheduled for a workshop or special meeting and noticed for final action.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated staff
  was working on an item regarding the sales tax waiver request.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Mayor Riggins discussed the permitting
  process for private water tanks and a Water District No. 29 water fee increase to
  fund improvements to the water system.

  Councilmember Conrad thanked staff for working with MRCA to remove the dead
  trees from the Malibu Bluffs.

  Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein suggested the schools make it mandatory for their
  students to participate in the safe driving program discussed by Mr. Shane.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated
  construction of the Permanent Skate Park had been delayed by the winter rains. He
  stated staff was still confirming whether a portion of the park could be opened in
  February 2026.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated there
  are some limits on the City's ability to regulate food trucks under State law.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein indicated support for a sales tax relief measure for fire
  rebuilds. He indicated support for scheduling the January 12, 2026 Item No. 8.A.
  report discussion for a special meeting. He requested consensus to form a Litigation
  Ad Hoc Committee to work with the City's counsel on litigation.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 9 of 12

  City Clerk Pettijohn explained restrictions on Ad Hoc Committees and
  Subcommittees.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein proposed bringing back an item to form a Litigation Ad
  Hoc Committee to work on all the City's existing litigation.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to consider forming
  a Litigation Ad Hoc Committee to work on all the City's existing litigation cases.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein, City Clerk Pettijohn explained that the
  Council had not formed a body to meet with the City's lobbyist, but that it was the
  City's practice to include the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tern in regular meetings.

  Mayor Riggins stated the City was working to complete the Permanent Skatepark
  as soon as possible and encouraged members of the public to wait for the official
  opening and not interfere with construction. She discussed community concerns
  regarding food trucks. She stated she met with Senator Irwin in Sacramento to
  discuss the sales tax issue and Malibu Unification, and that she attended the SM-
  MUSD Malibu Pathways event on Saturday.

RECESS  At 7:55 p.m., Mayor Riggins recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:10
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

  The Council discussed reordering the agenda and determined it would not reorder
  the agenda.

ITEM 5  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None.

ITEM 6  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Receive and File Update on Malibu's Community Lands (Continued from January
  12, 2026)
  Recommended Action: Receive and file an update on Malibu's Community Lands,
  and provide direction to staff as appropriate.

  Deputy City Manager Rojas and Community Services Director Riesgo presented
  the staff report.

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Kevin Keegan, Deanna Armbruster, Anne K., Jo Drummond, Alicia
  Peak, and Ryan
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 10 of 12

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Riggins returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Mayor Riggins seconded a motion to direct
  staff to bring back a plan for temporary sports fields on the 1oki Parcel, specifically
  including soccer fields.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Uhring moved to direct staff to work with the Use of Public Parks
  and Property Ad Hoc Committee on the plan for temporary fields.

  The maker and the seconder accepted the amendment.

  The amended motion carried 4-0, Councilmember Stewart absent.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion
  to direct staff to work with the Use of Public Parks and Property Ad Hoc Committee
  to explore options for a native plant nursery with the Santa Monica Mountains Fund
  and a potential communal garden.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff

  The motion,carried 4-0, Councilmember Stewart absent.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion
  to direct staff and the Use of Public Parks and Property Ad Hoc Committee to
  continue working on the Heathercliff project design and suspend work on the La
  Paz Parcel C project. The motion carried 3-1-0, Mayor Riggins opposed and
  Councilmember Stewart absent.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Mayor Riggins seconded a motion to direct
  staff to bring back an item at the March 23, 2026 Regular Meeting to discuss
  potentially swapping lands in the Civic Center Area with a private property owner.
  The motion carried 4-0, Councilmember Stewart absent.

MOTION  Mayor Riggins moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion to work
  with the Chamber of Commerce to explore building a Chamber office and
  information center on the Triangle Lot, along with parking.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 11 of 12

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  The motion failed 2-2-0, Councilmember Uhring and Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein
  opposed, Councilmember Stewart absent.

ITEM 7  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Rejection of Bids for the Malibu Community Labor Exchange Center Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Reject all bids received for the Malibu Community
  Labor Exchange Center Project, Specification No. 2103; and 2) Provide direction
  to staff on how to proceed.

  Assistant Public Works Director Holden presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Darrell Riley

  Anne K. was not available at the time of the hearing.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Riggins returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion
  to: 1) reject all bids received for the Malibu Community Labor Exchange Center
  Project, Specification No. 2103; and 2) direct staff to redesign the project and
  identify funding sources, not to including more than $250,000 from the General
  Fund, redesign is to include exploring relocating the project to the Triangle Parcel.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Riggins moved to direct staff to bring back a report with options for the
  project even if the General Fund costs would exceed $250,000.

  The maker and the seconder accepted the amendment.

  The amended motion carried 4-0, Councilmember Stewart absent.

ITEM 8  COUNCIL ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 26, 2026
  Page 12 of 12

  Mayor Riggins adjourned the meeting at 10:05 p.m.

  Approved and adopted by the City Council of the
  City of Malibu on A ust 24, 2026.

  BRUCE IiNERSTEIN, Mayor
